title: Linear Feature-Dimension Sweep
prompt:
Implement `double_descent_sweep(n_train, n_test, dimensions, noise_std=0.1, seed=0)` as a model-width experiment. Keep sample counts fixed and evaluate feature widths in their supplied order, including repeated widths. Assume positive train/test sizes, a nonempty sequence of positive integer widths, and nonnegative noise.

Generate one linear-Gaussian data realization with maximum width `P=max(dimensions)`. Use one local seeded NumPy generator to draw a length-P standard-normal weight vector, then train features, test features, train noise, and test noise, in that order. Targets use all P features and the shared weight vector. For width `p`, use the first p columns of those same feature matrices and the unchanged targets; do not redraw data per width. Fit the minimum-norm least-squares solution, without an intercept or ridge penalty. Return a list of `(p, train_mse, test_mse)` tuples. Repeated widths in the same sweep must have identical results, and changing only the width order must only reorder output.

Widths may exceed `n_train`; use a stable least-squares or pseudoinverse solver and compute MSE from predictions, since solver residual arrays may be empty for underdetermined systems. This measures a width sweep, not a guarantee that every finite seed produces a dramatic double-descent curve. It is distinct from the existing sample-wise experiment that varies training sample count.

example.output: three finite train/test MSE records in the requested order
example.reasoning: All widths evaluate nested views of one fixed data draw.
